reviewer_claims_the_controller_checked_a.claim: ap_launcher.py reads the manifest before checking it exists
reviewer_claims_the_controller_checked_a.finding: false. The code reads `candidate = global_manifest()` then `if os.path.isfile(candidate): manifest = candidate` -- manifest is only ever assigned when the file exists. The reviewer misread which branch the guard sits in

reviewer_claims_the_controller_checked_a.claim: _is_ancestor returns True for parent == child, so a launcher invoked from its own project root refuses its own manifest
reviewer_claims_the_controller_checked_a.finding: true of the equality case, and of no consequence. sibling_manifest is consulted only after the upward walk has already failed, and in the case described the candidate it would return is the same absent file the walk did not find. The docstring states this and calls it harmless

reviewer_claims_the_controller_checked_a.note: both sat in that reviewer's Critical/Important tiers. This is the loop-004-5 lesson holding: a confident citation is a prompt to verify, not evidence. Everything recorded above as reproduced was run by the controller

operational_findings.fan_out_concurrency: three fan-outs launched within 40 seconds produced 3 working panes of 10. The seven dead panes all carried revision 0, max_offset_from_bottom 0 and a cwd with a trailing backslash: herdr pane run never delivered. Re-running ONE fan-out at a time worked twice in a row. A second fan-out launched while the first was still starting failed identically, so the constraint is one fan-out at a time, not one launch at a time. fanout.sh discards pane run output, which is why the failure was silent
operational_findings.agy: never started in the security round and was not retried. CLAUDE.md records that agy auto-denies in headless mode the moment a tool needs the command permission, and collect.sh correctly refused to round a 0-byte reviewer up to a clean pass
